title: Eval Shepherd: probabilistic cohort prober and autotune threshold adapter
author: Anika Rao
release_notes: Add Eval Shepherd: a probabilistic cohort prober + adaptive CI threshold adapter that reduces false-positive regression fails for long-tail prompt cohorts. Includes CLI, CI hook, docs, and tests.
description:
Context and motivation: We observed intermittent CI failures caused by high-variance, low-volume cohorts in our prompt sets. These failures frequently required manual triage and slowed rollouts. This change introduces 'Eval Shepherd', a lightweight probabilistic prober and adaptive-threshold adapter intended to stabilize CI gating while preserving sensitivity to real regressions.

What this PR does: Implements a cohort prober that samples prompts probabilistically across defined cohort strata, computes a per-cohort stability score (variance-aware fidelity metric), and uses a small Bayesian bootstrap autotuner to adjust CI gate thresholds per run. Adds a pressure-aware latch for CI (defer hard fail until variance and effective-sample-size criteria are met), a local CLI for devs to run sanity probes, and a webhook reporter that surfaces cohort-level anomalies to the eval dashboard.

Design notes: The probe intentionally favors stratified stochastic sampling rather than exhaustive replay so CI remains fast. The autotuner computes posterior credible intervals for the metric delta and only tightens the failure threshold when posterior mass exceeds caller-configured risk tolerance. The pressure latch implements a backoff that increases sampling budget when transient noise is detected.

Files and surface area changed: core shepherd runtime, a CI hook, a small CLI, unit/integration tests, docs, and an example probe config. No runtime-serving changes.

How it was tested: Unit tests for Bayesian estimator and latch (deterministic seeds), integration smoke runs against a three-model matrix (tiny/local mocks), and a staged run on the canary CI agent against a representative prompt snapshot.

Checklist:
- [x] Core probe implementation with deterministic unit tests
- [x] CI hook + config for pressure-aware latch
- [x] CLI for local repro and example config
- [x] Integration test with mocked eval backends
- [x] Documentation and rollout notes

Operational considerations: Default autotune parameters are conservative; rollout will start as a soft-fail (warning) in CI before promoting to hard-fail after two weeks. The webhook includes cohort fingerprints for triage and links to the snapshot used for the probe.

Migration path and rollout plan: Feature gated behind experiment flag in ci/configs/sentinel.yml. Enable soft-fail for two weeks, monitor cohort flood events and manual triage latency, then flip to hard-fail when pilot metrics show >30% reduction in false-positive CI incidents.

Related work: INGESTED from previous regressions analysis (ENG-1029); complements the context-length-aware regression gate (separate PR).

Notes for reviewers: Pay attention to the Bayesian credible-interval defaults and the effective-sample-size (ESS) calculations in shepherd/core/estimator.py. The autotuner is intentionally small (no external deps beyond numpy/scipy) to keep CI startup light.
